meta.title: Students' Voice & Student Rep Elections
meta.note: Content sourced from the Year 2 / L3 variant of this deck (see SOURCE_OF_TRUTH note in the PowerPoint's teacher appendix). Swap when a true Year 1 deck is provided.

questions.prompt: Which PROUD value is Module D grounded in?
questions.explanation: Module D is grounded in Encourage Unity.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an example of feedback that 'names the thing'?
options: 'Things would be good if they were better'
questions.explanation: 'Four edit stations can't run Premiere' beats 'the software is rubbish'.

questions.prompt: Which are the four 'ways to get involved' in the deck? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: All four are the ways to get involved.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Students' Voice?
options: Giving students influence over college improvements
questions.explanation: Giving students influence over college improvements

questions.prompt: How many Student Governor places are on the Main Governing Board?
questions.explanation: There are 3 Student Governor places on the Main Governing Board.

questions.prompt: Which of these are examples of useful, specific feedback? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: "Four edit stations cannot run Premiere." names the thing and is useful feedback.

questions.prompt: How does the deck describe the difference between one person's complaint and a group's view?
options: One is an opinion; a group saying the same thing is evidence - and evidence is what changes decisions
A single complaint carries more weight than a group
questions.explanation: One person's complaint is an opinion. A group saying the same thing is evidence - and evidence is what changes decisions.

questions.prompt: Which are stages of the election in the deck? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: All four are the stages: Nominations -> Pitches -> Vote -> Confirm & register.
